subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — SLO triggers, maintenance carve-outs, and credit matrix
messages:
From: Samantha Ruiz <samantha.ruiz@alphatech.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Holden <m.holden@alphatech.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA redlines — uptime SLOs, credits, and maintenance carve-outs

Connor — thanks for sharing the draft Order Form and MSA. Procurement reviewed the SLA and attached our redline set (AlphaTech_SLA_Redlines_v1.docx). High-level asks: 

- Uptime: we need 99.99% for production API endpoints (monthly). Your draft at 99.95% exceeds our risk tolerance.
- Service credits: request a step-down credit matrix that scales for >0.25% and >0.5% monthly downtime. Please confirm the maximum credit cap and whether credits are refundable vs. apply to future invoices.
- Response times: we expect P1 acknowledgement within 1 hour and initial remediation ETA within 4 hours for SEV1. Your proposed 2-hour acknowledge/8-hour ETA is a blocker for finance.
- Maintenance carve-outs: we need a carve-out definition for scheduled maintenance not to exceed 4 hours per month per region and a 72-hour advance notice for non-emergency maintenance; your current language is broader.

Can we get Redwood's position on each item by end of week? We are trying to get procurement sign-off for the Q2 deployment. I can set up a quick call if needed — Marcus and I are available Thursday afternoon PST.

Thanks,
Samantha Ruiz
Sr. Procurement Manager | AlphaTech Inc.
Attachment: AlphaTech_SLA_Redlines_v1.docx (docx)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ruiz <samantha.ruiz@alphatech.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA redlines — uptime SLOs, credits, and maintenance carve-outs

Samantha — appreciate the clear redlines and prompt review. I pulled in Lauren (legal) and Aditya (sales/finance) to help, and we attached a counter with compromise language (Redwood_SLA_Counter_v2.pdf). High-level position below; see inline comments in the PDF for mapping to your doc.

Summary responses:
- Uptime: we can agree to 99.99% for the primary production endpoint if AlphaTech commits to a 12-month minimum spend on Dedicated or a 6-month commit on Hosted with a usage collar. Without a commitment we would need to remain at 99.95% (our standard).
- Service credits: propose a three-tier matrix: 5% credit for monthly availability <99.95%, 10% credit for <99.9%, 20% credit for <99.5% with a 75% cap of monthly invoice for credits. Credits are applied to future invoices (not cash refunds) for commercial customers — we can discuss cash refunds for enterprise agreements.
- Response times: for SEV1 we can shorten acknowledgement to 1 hour and initial ETA to 6 hours if AlphaTech is on our enterprise on-call rotation (shared contact and escalation path). Otherwise we keep 2/8. We want to avoid guaranteed remediation SLAs that require on-call staffing profiles; acknowledgement/ETA are OK.
- Maintenance carve-outs: we can accept a 4-hour monthly scheduled maintenance cap per region with 72-hour notice for non-emergency maintenance. We need language for blackout windows during AlphaTech's high-traffic events to avoid accidental upgrades.

Next steps: Lauren will propose revised MSA text for these items by EOD 4/21. If AlphaTech can confirm intended commitment profile (Dedicated vs Hosted + term), Aditya will provide the pricing offsets. Happy to run a 30-min sync Thu 4/22 2pm PT if that works for you.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Counter_v2.pdf

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ruiz <samantha.ruiz@alphatech.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T15:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA redlines — uptime SLOs, credits, and maintenance carve-outs

Samantha / Connor — looping in Kimberly (legal ops) for carve-out and notice language. Attached below are the specific MSA/Order Form redlines we propose; I included rationale to help your legal team. Key changes in-line: 

1) Definitions: we define "Availability" as platform ingress + model inference for production endpoints; measurement excludes scheduled maintenance and customer-caused incidents (we included a short list of examples).

2) Uptime commitment: we will accept 99.99% if AlphaTech signs a 12-month Dedicated commitment OR 6-month Hosted commitment with a minimal guaranteed spend. If AlphaTech cannot commit, Redwood will remain at 99.95%. This is non-negotiable because of multi-tenant capacity planning and reserved GPU scheduling.

3) Credit matrix: we propose credits applied as account-level invoice credits only. Example language included: credit tiers at <99.95%, <99.9%, <99.5% with a 75% cap of the monthly bill. We are open to a negotiated cash refund clause for enterprise customers with signed SOC2+ additional indemnities; that would be a separate SOW.

4) Response times / SEV definitions: accept 1-hour acknowledgement and commitment to provide a remediation ETA within 6 hours for SEV1 when customer provides a 24/7 on-call contact and follows the incident escalation procedure. Our legal team cannot accept a binding "fix within X hours" remediation SLA because remediation depends on root-cause.

5) Maintenance carve-outs & blackouts: agreed 4 hours/month per region for scheduled maintenance with 72-hour notice. We added a clause for mutually agreed blackout windows (AlphaTech to provide dates 30 days in advance for major events).

Please confirm if the carve-out and blackout language is acceptable. If AlphaTech wants cash credit alternatives or removal of the commit requirement for 99.99%, that will need commercial review.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-04-25T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA redlines — uptime SLOs, credits, and maintenance carve-outs

Thanks, Lauren and team — this is helpful and much clearer. A few clarifications before we proceed to signatures: 

- Commitment profile: AlphaTech prefers Hosted with a 6-month minimum spend (we can share an expected monthly usage band later today). That should meet your condition for 99.99% per your note.
- Credits: applying to future invoices is acceptable to us; we will confirm with Finance on cash refund exceptions and flag if we need an enterprise cash option.
- Response times: we will provide the 24/7 on-call contact and follow your incident escalation process to enable the 1-hr acknowledgement / 6-hr ETA path. Please add the escalation contact fields to the Order Form.
- Blackouts: we will send a list of Q3 product launch blackout dates by 5/1.

Next steps: can Redwood produce a redline PDF that incorporates the agreed items (u99.99 with 6m Hosted commit, credits applied to invoices, 1/6 response path with on-call contact, maintenance carve-outs + blackout wording)? If yes, we can route to our legal and procurement for final review and then request DocuSign. Marcus is on copy and will coordinate final procurement steps.

If you can get the updated redline by EOD Monday 4/26 we can stay on track for May deployment.

Regards,
Samantha Ruiz
Sr. Procurement Manager | AlphaTech Inc.
